Author: Subhash Chandra Sharma
Bench: Subhash Chandra Sharma
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 82
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 917 of 2023
Applicant :- Jai Prakash Mishra

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Shri Prakash Dwivedi
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Shashi Ranjan Srivastava
Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Heard Sri Prakash Dwivedi, learned learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Shashi Ranjan Srivastava,
learned counsel for opposite party as learned A.G.A and perused the record.
The instant Anticipatory Bail Application has been filed by the applicant with a prayer to grant an
anticipatory bail to the applicant in Case Crime No.210 of 2022, under sections 419, 420, 467, 468,
406, 506 I.P.C, Police Station Marihan, District Mirzapur.
Facts in brief are that in this case the informant went with co-accused Kailash Nath Tripathi at the instance of present applicant to purchase land illegally in the village Khachaha.
Hetransferred Rs.56,50,000/- in the account of co-accused Kailash Nath Tripathi on 18.8.2018.

The informant was taken to the Registrar office where on 18.8.2018 sale deed was prepared and Rs.5,00,000/- in cash were also taken by the accused person and did not execute the sale deed but both of them went away from there.

Later on it was found thatin khatauni relating the fasali year 1412 to 1417 the co-accused got his name registered fraudulently and made sale deed of the land in favour of several persons prior to the present incident.
When the informant asked to refund the money he was intimidated by the co-accused.

sentences.text: It is submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant that he is innocent and has committed no offence.
No money was transferred in his account and the land also did not belong to him.
His role is only to meet the informant to the co-accused Kailash Nath Tripathi from whom land was to be bought.
It is also submitted that the applicant introduced the informant with co-accused Kailash Nath Tripathi.
Therefore, no offence is made out against the applicant.
Since the investigation is going on and there appears apprehension of arrest of applicant, so request for anticipatory bail.
Learned A.G.A opposed the aforesaid prayer and urged that co-accused Kailash Nath Tripathi was working in collusion of present applicant.
He was also present in the Registry office on 18.8.2018 but after receiving the amount, the applicant and co-accused fled away from there without executing the sale deed.
Even, the money was also not refunded to him.
It is also urged that there is criminal case of similar nature against the present applicant which shows that the applicant has committed the offence.
Therefore, he is not entitled for anticipatory bail.

On considering the facts and circumstances of the case and submissions made by the learned counsel for the applicant, learned counsel for opposite party as well as learned A.G.A for the State and perusal of record, there appears no ground for anticipatory bail, hence the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is hereby rejected.

However, as per submission made by learned counsel for the applicant, in case the applicant appears and moves bail application before the concerned Court, it shall be heard and disposed of as expeditiously as possible in accordance with law.
Order Date :- 23.3.2023 G.S
